item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a camera watching a quiet hallway. For several seconds, almost every part of the scene stays the same.

item.title: 1.2 Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation
item.description: Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation With the basic structure of a spiking neural network in place, imagine its input changing over a short interval.

item.title: 1.3 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron A spike event gives a spiking neural network a precisely timed signal, but a neuron still needs a rule for deciding when to produce that event.

item.title: 1.4 From Input Signals to Network Spikes
item.description: From Input Signals to Network Spikes A spike train gives a spiking neuron a sequence of events to process, and a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron turns those arriving events into its own outgoing spikes.

item.title: 1.5 Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition
item.description: Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition Once an input has been encoded as spikes and those spikes have begun propagating through a network, several neurons may receive evidence at nearly the same time.

item.title: 1. From Spiking Neural Network to Brain-inspired Computation
3.1 Classification Accuracy
item.description: Classification Accuracy Once a spiking neural network has produced a predicted class label, evaluation begins by comparing that prediction with the target class label-the correct answer attached to the input.
